claims.text: A narrow scalar example is an index {sensorId: 1, ts: -1} serving an equality filter on sensorId, descending ts order, and projection {sensorId: 1, ts: 1, _id: 0}; adding a requested field absent from that index requires fetching documents. (high confidence)

Projection reduces returned data and network traffic, but document reads disappear only when a covered plan can answer the query from an index; an IXSCAN followed by FETCH still reads collection documents. (high confidence)

For ordinary scalar-field coverage, the fields needed by the query and the returned fields must be available from the same index. Explicitly exclude _id when it is absent from that index; an index that includes _id can instead return it without violating this requirement. (high confidence)

find() and $project include _id by default. If the candidate covering index omits _id, explicitly project _id: 0; otherwise retrieving _id can force a document fetch even when every other requested field is indexed. (high confidence)

Verify coverage with explain execution statistics and the actual winning plan: an index-only plan has no document-fetch ancestor of its index scan, and totalDocsExamined should be zero. An IXSCAN by itself is insufficient because a FETCH can sit above it. (high confidence)

A $match filter independent of projected computations can move ahead of projection stages; a filter on a computed result cannot simply move before the stage that computes it. This constrains assumptions about index access when shaping output. (low confidence)

find() sorts on original field values before applying projection. Aggregation stage order and optimizer dependencies matter: a $sort preceded by $project can lose index-backed sorting, and moving a computed projection across sort plus limit can change which documents raise errors. (high confidence)

In its update dated 2026-10-22, SERVER-135176 reports a presence-sensitive aggregation example where projection pushdown makes an indexed pipeline return $type as null for a missing field; the index-free pipeline returns missing. The report does not identify affected or fixed release versions, so it cannot establish a release-wide exposure range. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-22)

For the scalar inclusion examples, explain("executionStats") distinguishes PROJECTION_COVERED over IXSCAN with totalDocsExamined: 0 from a projection over FETCH and IXSCAN with positive document examinations. Inspect actual executions with matching data rather than equating index use with coverage. (high confidence)

MongoDB issue SERVER-134945 reports a reproducer where adding $count enables covered input and changes a downstream missing-field match result because an absent indexed path is materialized as null. Treat this as a reported correctness edge case, and verify missing-versus-null behavior on the deployed build rather than generalizing it to all versions. (low confidence)

SERVER-54128 documents a historical correctness bug where a computed projection pushed before sort plus limit could raise an error on a document that the original pipeline would discard. The issue describes pushing required input fields instead of eagerly evaluating the computed projection. (low confidence)

Aggregation can also use a covering index for its input-stage query. Coverage is a property of the optimized dependencies and selected plan, so replacing find projection with $project does not by itself establish or eliminate coverage. The API comparison is an inference from the documented find coverage rules and aggregation index support. (high confidence)

Current documented find projection accepts aggregation expressions, including computing new fields and replacing existing field values. The older blanket distinction that only aggregation $project can compute output fields is therefore inaccurate. (low confidence)

Both find projection and aggregation $project support inclusion, exclusion, computed values, and default inclusion of _id. Their overlapping output capabilities do not guarantee identical execution plans. (medium confidence)

MongoDB automatically determines the subset of document fields needed by an aggregation pipeline. Adding an early or middle $project solely to reduce fields passed downstream is usually unlikely to improve performance; $project typically belongs at the end to select client output. (high confidence)

A production write-up traced unnecessary document reads to a Spring Data include projection that implicitly retained _id. Explicitly excluding _id removed the document-fetch work, while repeated index values still crossed the network; coverage alone did not remove that remaining work. (medium confidence)

A covered query obtains its predicate inputs and returned fields from the same index without examining collection documents. All required fields, including fields needed internally, must be available; null-equality predicates are a documented restriction. (high confidence)

Since MongoDB 4.4, find projections accept aggregation expressions and can create or replace output fields. An old statement that computed projections require the $project pipeline stage is not a valid modern API distinction. (high confidence)
